EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by aliphatic C–H features (strong CH stretches at 2933/2863 cm⁻¹ per GFQ-003, and CH₂ bending near 1448 cm⁻¹ per GFQ-003), plus a carbonyl around 1698 cm⁻¹ consistent with a saturated carboxylic acid/acid-type carbonyl rather than an ester (which is typically higher) or amide/imine (which would show NH/C=N signatures). The pronounced CH₂ rocking region with peaks at ~725/750 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of longer aliphatic chains, favoring the more extended branched acid in candidate 1 over shorter/other functionalities. Additional mid-frequency bands (1103, 1286, ~1000 cm⁻¹) fit C–C/C–O skeletal and CH₂ wag/twist typical of aliphatic acids.
